plan.planning_summary: The problem defines a strictly constrained two-layer antireflection coating design space with only one genuine degree of freedom: the permutation of the two required materials (SiO2 and TiO2). Since the topology fixes the layer count to exactly two and the material set to exactly one of each, there are only two possible stack configurations: [Air/SiO2/TiO2/Glass] and [Air/TiO2/SiO2/Glass]. These represent mutually exclusive discrete states; a single optimization route cannot tune 'order' as a continuous variable without becoming a combinatorial search that obscures which specific topology yielded the result. Therefore, the strategy selects the single most physically promising axis based on standard AR coating theory (gradient index matching) to maximize the probability of meeting the soft target within the limited evaluation budget. The chosen axis optimizes the thicknesses of the Low-High (SiO2-TiO2) configuration, hypothesizing that placing the lower index material first provides a smoother impedance transition from air to the high-index titania layer and finally to the glass substrate.

routes.title: Optimization of SiO2/TiO2 Bilayer Order and Thickness for Broadband AR
routes.scientific_hypothesis: For a two-layer system with indices n_air < n_SiO2 < n_TiO2 > n_glass, the stack ordering Air/SiO2/TiO2/Glass yields a lower global minimum mean reflectance than Air/TiO2/SiO2/Glass because the intermediate SiO2 layer reduces the initial impedance mismatch at the air interface more effectively than starting with the high-index TiO2.
routes.design_principle: Impedance matching in multilayer optics suggests that arranging layers in ascending order of refractive index (or close to it) minimizes Fresnel reflections at each interface. Placing the lower index SiO2 (n=1.46) adjacent to air (n=1.0) creates a smaller step change than placing TiO2 (n=2.40) adjacent to air, potentially broadening the low-reflectance bandwidth despite the non-ideal final step from TiO2 to Glass (n=1.52).
soft_objectives: minimize arithmetic mean power reflectance (s-pol, normal incidence) over 450-700 nm
achieve mean reflectance below 0.03 as a preference
manufacturing_considerations: layer thicknesses must remain within 40 nm to 160 nm bounds
exactly one layer of each material permitted
theory_basis: Fresnel equations for normal incidence reflection at dielectric interfaces
Transfer Matrix Method (TMM) for calculating coherent superposition of fields in stratified media
Quarter-wave transformer theory generalized for broadband minimization via numerical optimization
expected_advantages: Directly tests the theoretically preferred material ordering for impedance grading
Concentrates the limited 64-evaluation budget on refining thicknesses for the most promising topology rather than splitting resources between two topologies
Provides a clear baseline; if this optimal ordering fails to meet the target, the reverse ordering is unlikely to succeed given the larger initial index mismatch
known_risks: The reverse order (TiO2/SiO2) might unexpectedly perform better due to specific phase cancellation effects at the substrate interface not captured by simple impedance arguments
The thickness constraints (40-160 nm) may prevent the formation of ideal quarter-wave or half-wave conditions for the entire 450-700 nm band
Constant index assumption may introduce errors if actual material dispersion is significant, though the problem statement mandates constant indices
routes.execution_request_english: Execute a deterministic Transfer Matrix Method (TMM) optimization for a planar four-medium stack: Air (n=1.0), Layer 1 (SiO2 (Gao), n=1.46), Layer 2 (TiO2 (Siefke), n=2.40), Substrate (Glass, n=1.52). The optimization must vary the thickness of the SiO2 (Gao) layer and the TiO2 (Siefke) layer independently, subject to hard bounds of 40 nm to 160 nm for each. The objective function is the arithmetic mean of the power reflectance for s-polarized light at normal incidence (0 degrees), calculated at 5 nm intervals from 450 nm to 700 nm inclusive. Use a deterministic optimizer with seed 17, allowing a maximum of 64 solver evaluations. Report the best candidate's thicknesses, the full reflectance spectrum, and the calculated mean reflectance. Do not use RCWA, FDFD, or surrogate models.

unresolved_decisions: Whether the reverse topology (Air/TiO2/SiO2/Glass) should be tested in a subsequent study if route_01 fails to achieve a mean reflectance below 0.05, as the current budget allows only one route.
plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: If the single executed route yields a mean reflectance greater than 0.05 despite exhaustive tuning within bounds, conclude that a two-layer system with these specific materials and thickness constraints is insufficient to meet the 0.03 target, and recommend expanding the design space to three layers or relaxing thickness limits in future work.
